issues.claim: without a finalizer the resource stays held until the process ends
issues.problem: This holds only for OS handles that the OS reclaims at process exit. A resource outside the process (a remote lock, a temp file, a database connection) may never be cleaned up. Stating it as a general rule is misleading, and the answer hinge itself says 'or leak'. The cited excerpts do not support the 'until process end' claim.
issues.suggestedFix: EN: 'without a finalizer the resource is not released by the garbage collector at all and leaks (an OS handle is reclaimed at most when the process exits)'. RU: 'без финализатора сборщик мусора ресурс не освободит вовсе, он утечёт (дескриптор ОС в лучшем случае закроется при завершении процесса)'. Apply the same softening in answer and explanation, in both locales.

issues.claim: the finalizer runs later on a separate thread; BCL types usually keep handles in a SafeHandle, which has a finalizer, so the handle is eventually closed, but until then the file may stay locked
issues.problem: The fetched excerpts show that the GC does not call Dispose and that Dispose(false) is the finalizer path. They do not show the finalizer-thread claim or the SafeHandle/FileStream claim that the file stays locked until finalization. The generator's notes admit these were not checked against the pages. The claims are true as far as I know, but the cited sources do not demonstrate them in the excerpts.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.object.finalize and the SafeHandle documentation for these claims, or shorten the sentence to what the cited pages support.

issues.claim: Option b is two to three times longer than the other options
issues.problem: The much longer option b is the correct one, so its length signals the right answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten option b to roughly the length of the others, for example: 'The garbage collector does not call Dispose. A finalizer, if the type has one, may release the resource later; otherwise the resource leaks.'

issues.claim: Even ReadyToRun precompilation adds machine code next to the IL, not instead of it.
issues.problem: This is true as far as I know: R2R images keep IL and metadata alongside the native code. Neither cited page, as fetched, mentions ReadyToRun, so the claim has no cited support. The generator's notes also ask for confirmation.
issues.suggestedFix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/ready-to-run as a third link (with linkTitles in both locales) to support the claim, or remove the ReadyToRun sentence from option b's explanation.
